body.p: In this amendment, claims 1, 3-10, 12-18, 21, and 22 are pending, with claims 1, 10, and 21 being independent. Claims 1, 3, 4, 7-10, 12, 13, 16-18, 21, and 22 are amended. Claims 2, 11, 19, and 20 are canceled. Support for these amendments can be found at least in paragraphs 35, 36, and 41, and in FIGS. 1 and 2A of Applicant's disclosure. No new matter has been added.

Applicant acknowledges, with appreciation, Examiners Park and Henson for participating in the telephonic interview (Interview) conducted on August 29, 2024, with the undersigned. During the Interview, no exhibit was shown, and no demonstration was conducted. Potential amendments to claim 1 were discussed in connection with the rejection under § 102. No agreement was reached during the Interview.

Claims 3-4 and 12-13 have been objected to over a typographical error. Within claims 3-4 and 12-13, the term "breath" has been replaced with "breathe." Accordingly, withdrawal of the objection to claims 3-4 and 12-13 is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-18 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2021/0150873 to Shouldice et al. (Shouldice) in view of U.S. Publication No. 2019/0038179 to Tanriover et al. (Tanriover).
Amended claim 1 recites, in part:
passively monitoring the user's breathing with a device during a
predetermined time interval generating sensor-generated signals, wherein the sensor-generated signals include acoustic signals comprising audio and motion
signals;
detecting a plurality of phases of the user's breathing by processing solely
the audio of the acoustic signals using a machine learning model;
wherein the machine learning model is trained as a student model in a

teacher-student architecture including a teacher model configured to teach the machine learning model by generating labels for received motion training data corresponding to human breathing, wherein the machine learning model uses the
labels during a training process to learn to classify training audio corresponding to the human breathing into the plurality of phases, and wherein the training audio is
time aligned with the motion training data;
identifying a breathing mode of the user's breathing and detecting that the

breathing mode is a particular trigger mode selected from a plurality of detectable trigger modes including shallow breathing and mouth breathing by processing data created from the sensor-generated signals and the plurality of phases of the user's breathing using a further machine learning model trained, at least in part, to
distinguish between shallow breathing and mouth breathing; and
responsive to detecting the trigger mode, providing to the user via the device
real time biofeedback specifying a breathing exercise adapted to the particular
trigger mode.

Amended claim 1 incorporates subject matter from dependent claim 2 pertaining to the training of the machine learning model. As amended, claim 1 clarifies that "phases of the user's breathing" are detected "by processing solely audio of the acoustic signals using a machine learning model." See, e.g., FIG. 1 classifier 106 including ML model 108 and 1 35 of Applicant's disclosure. The machine learning model is trained using a student-teacher model in which the teacher model operates on motion training data corresponding to human breathing to generate labels that are provided to the machine learning model. The machine learning model learns to classify training audio corresponding to human breathing into the different phases based on the labels provided from the teacher model. See, e.g., FIG. 2A illustrating the student-teacher architecture and 11 36 and 41.

Amended claim 1 addresses a technological challenge relating to the difficulty in accurately annotating acoustic data due to inaudible boundaries of breathing phases by delineating these phases using motion signals and then training audio processing based on the motion signals. See, e.g., 1 42 of Applicant's disclosure. Applicant respectfully submits that Shouldice and Tanriover, whether considered individually or in combination, do not disclose or suggest the features recited by amended claim 1.
Applicant's remarks supporting patentability of claim 1 are relevant to independent claim 10 and are hereby reiterated in support thereof.
The remaining claims rejected under § 103 in view Shouldice and Tanriover are believed to be allowable in view of their own merits and their dependence on the underlying base claims.
In view of the foregoing, withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejection of claims 1-18 is respectfully requested.
Claims 21-22 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being allegedly anticipated by Shouldice.
Independent claim 21 is amended to clarify certain features relating to the training of the first machine learning model. As amended, claim 21 recites, in part:
training a first machine learning model as a student model in a teacher- student architecture to detect a plurality of breathing phases by:
generating labels corresponding to the plurality of breathing phases using a teacher model configured to operate on motion training data
corresponding to human breathing;

teaching the first machine learning model to classify training audio into the plurality of breathing phases based on the labels from the teacher model, wherein the training audio corresponds to the human breathing and
is time aligned with the motion training data;
passively monitoring a user's breathing by detecting audio with an acoustic
sensor of a device; and
detecting breathing phases of the user's breathing by processing the audio
using the first machine learning model as trained.

Applicant respectfully submits that claim 21 patentably defines over the cited reference as Shouldice does not disclose or suggest the features relating to training using a teacher-student architecture.
Claim 22 is believed to patentably define over Shouldice in view of its own merits and its dependence on claim 21.
Accordingly, withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) rejection of claims 21-22 is respectfully requested.

Reconsideration and a Notice of Allowance are respectfully requested in view of the amended claims and the Remarks presented above. If there are any questions, a telephone call to the undersigned is invited.
Respectfully submitted,
